checks.name: packets came out of the encoder
checks.why: every percentile and the effective rate in this run is computed over these packets, so a run that produced none makes each of those figures an absence rather than a number

checks.name: every submitted frame came back
checks.why: Opus is lossy in amplitude and exact in length, so a decoded length that disagrees with the submitted one is a defect and not a tolerance; the population is the submitted frames, because two counts of nothing agree perfectly

checks.name: encode p99 under a tenth of the frame
checks.why: a tenth of the 5 ms frame is 500 us, and an encoder under that cannot be the term that matters in a budget measured in whole milliseconds; p99 rather than the mean, because a frame late once every hundred is a click a listener hears

checks.name: the left channel decodes to its own tone
checks.why: a byte count and a frame count agree just as happily when the decoder returns silence, and this project has read that agreement as success; 997 Hz comes out of the decoded samples, at a window resolution of 2 Hz

checks.name: the right channel decodes to its own tone
checks.why: the two channels carry different frequencies so that channel order is provable rather than assumed, and a right channel reading 997 Hz is what a swap looks like

checks.name: the decoded channels stay distinct
checks.why: two channels reading one frequency is consistent with a fold to mono, with one channel encoded twice, and with a detector measuring its own scratch buffer, and a frame count is consistent with all three

findings: a 5 ms frame carries 81 byte packets at 129.7 kbps effective against the 128 kbps asked for
